meta.name: SwarmLabs Grand Challenge Ledger
meta.purpose: Track world-hard-problem breakthroughs by AI in math/physics/experimental science; score what SwarmLabs can realistically attack; feed weekly_iteration_report.
meta.evidence_rule: Every milestone entry MUST carry a primary-source URL. No milestone without a link.

verified_milestones.event: First end-to-end Lean formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem: 11 days, ~13M lines Lean, 30,300 theorems proved / 29,500 used, only 3 standard axioms, ~6B output tokens, internal model ~Claude Fable 5.1. Kevin Buzzard independently compiled and verified.
verified_milestones.nature: FORMALIZATION of a known 1995 proof (Wiles) — NOT new math
verified_milestones.signal: Autoformalization of modern math literature is now engineering-feasible; verification of AI-generated math becomes industrial.

verified_milestones.event: Solved 9 OPEN Erdős problems (2 open for 56 years) + 44 OEIS conjectures + 1 15-year algebraic geometry problem, all Lean-verified. Cost $200-600 per problem.
verified_milestones.nature: NEW MATH — genuinely open problems solved, machine-checked
verified_milestones.signal: Open research-level problem solving is now affordable; success concentrated where Mathlib is mature (combinatorics/number theory).

verified_milestones.event: Formalized Viazovska's Fields-Medal sphere-packing proofs (E8 d=8, Leech d=24) in ~2 weeks; d=24 alone ~180k lines. CAUGHT AND FIXED 2 SUBTLE ERRORS in the original human arguments.
verified_milestones.nature: FORMALIZATION + error discovery in published human proof
verified_milestones.signal: Direct precedent for SwarmLabs' strongest opening: machines finding real errors in PUBLISHED results. In math the verifier is Lean; in experimental science the verifier is ground-truth replication — our engine's home turf.

verified_milestones.event: FrontierMath Tier 4 at 97.6% (benchmark saturated; Epoch AI notes OpenAI funded the benchmark and holds exclusive access to some items). Internal model produced 10 formal results for ~$2000 tokens in Aug.
verified_milestones.nature: BENCHMARK SCORE — not independently re-verified deliverables
verified_milestones.signal: Benchmark scores and verifiable deliverables are different currencies; verifiable artifacts (Lean files, replicated experiments) carry more trust weight.

candidate_challenges.name: Published-Result Refutation Engine (实验科学版 Gauss)
candidate_challenges.thesis: Gauss caught 2 real errors in a Fields-Medal proof by formal re-verification. The experimental-science analog: re-run published kinetics/growth/physics results through our virtual experiment engine and machine-check them against the paper's own data. Errors found = headline-grade evidence, zero lab cost.
assets_we_already_have: engine/paper_validation.py: 14 papers / 18 benchmarks / 130 data points, mean r=0.957 (3 PASS / 10 MARGINAL / 0 FAIL)
52 microbiology scenarios w/ published formulas + references (data/microbiology_scenarios.json)
UQ machinery (GP surrogate, coverage calibration, noise-floor 3%)
candidate_challenges.upgrade_needed: Flip the harness from 'replicate' to 'adversarial audit': for each paper, formally flag which fitted parameters are UNIDENTIFIABLE, which predictions have CI overlapping the paper's error bars, and which conclusions are NOT SUPPORTED at stated noise floors. Output a machine-checkable 'audit certificate' per paper.
candidate_challenges.verifiability: HIGH — conclusions are computationally re-checkable from published data
candidate_challenges.novelty: HIGH — nobody is doing 'refutation-as-a-service' for experimental papers; the FLT moment makes verification bottlenecks a mainstream story
candidate_challenges.fit_with_swarmlabs: DIRECT — this is our UQ moat pointed at a real target
candidate_challenges.first_action: Add an AUDIT mode to paper_validation.py that emits explicit refutation flags (identifiability failures / coverage violations) instead of only r-scores; start with the 10 MARGINAL benchmarks already in hand.

candidate_challenges.name: Lean-for-Lab-Claims: machine-checkable certificates for AI-proposed experiments
candidate_challenges.thesis: FLT proves verification of AI-generated math is the bottleneck story of 2026. The same gap exists in experimental science: agents now PROPOSE experiments, but nothing machine-checks whether a proposed design can actually support its claimed conclusion (identifiability, power, coverage). Our guard + UQ is exactly that checker.
assets_we_already_have: Agent Skills distribution channel (K-Dense-AI model, 163-skill marketplace reference)
candidate_challenges.upgrade_needed: Package 'experiment-claim verification' as a skill/MCP tool: agent proposes experiment -> tool returns VERIFIED/REFUTED/UNDERDETERMINED with coverage math. Machine-checkable, like a Lean kernel verdict, but for designs.
candidate_challenges.verifiability: HIGH — verdict is computed, not asserted
candidate_challenges.novelty: HIGH — 'verification layer for agentic science' rides the exact 2026 narrative (trust in agentic workflows) that Catalyst Grant theme names
candidate_challenges.fit_with_swarmlabs: DIRECT — reuses our existing agent-infra work + aishield MCP distribution muscle
candidate_challenges.first_action: Wrap engine/guard.py + surrogate coverage check into one MCP tool 'verify_experiment_claim' with a three-verdict output schema; ship as aishield-adjacent skill.

candidate_challenges.name: Identifiability of microbial kinetics parameters (Monod/Haldane/Contois)
candidate_challenges.thesis: Well-posed open-ish computational question: for which experimental designs are Monod-family parameters structurally/practically unidentifiable? Publishable as a benchmark paper; directly extends our 52-scenario coverage.
candidate_challenges.upgrade_needed: Profile-based identifiability analysis (Fisher information / profile likelihood) per scenario; emit an identifiability atlas as open data.
candidate_challenges.novelty: MEDIUM — solid but incremental; good paper, not a 'world problem'
candidate_challenges.first_action: Add profile-likelihood identifiability scoring to microbiology_full.py; run over 52 scenarios; publish atlas JSON.

candidate_challenges.name: Formal math (Lean) proof race
candidate_challenges.thesis: Chase FLT-style formalization or open Erdős problems ourselves.
candidate_challenges.reason: Needs frontier-scale models (6B output tokens for FLT), Lean/mathlib infra and multi-agent proof harnesses. Our stack is pure numpy on a 32GB no-GPU box. Zero probability of contributing at the frontier; would burn focus.

candidate_challenges.name: Physics grand challenges (fusion, materials discovery, protein design)
candidate_challenges.thesis: A-Lab-style autonomous materials discovery or protein design.
candidate_challenges.reason: Needs real labs, DFT/MD simulation stacks and domain teams we do not have. Our engine covers heat1d-class PDE toy problems only. Watch, do not enter.

No problem-ledger discipline: competitor monitoring tracks products, not breakthroughs. This ledger adds the missing lane.
GEO opportunity: GC-01/GC-02 outputs (audit certificates, error findings) are exactly the kind of verifiable artifacts LLM engines cite. Each refutation finding = citable content.
